page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 12 dedicated vCPUs derived from 6 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The processor topology includes hyperthreading with two threads per core, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache and hardware vector extensions including AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512_VNNI. System RAM totals 24.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps, includes no attached local disk storage, features no GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance data reveals a distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded execution capabilities. Single-core performance benchmarks place the instance in lower tiers, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1310.99 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 22.76 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-threaded benchmarks demonstrate middle-tier efficiency, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 10472.88, a Geekbench multi-core score of 5894.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 11934.41. Uncached memory throughput reaches 71.19 GB/sec for large block reads and 42.85 GB/sec for large block writes.

The absence of local ephemeral disk storage requires reliance on network-attached storage for persistent workloads. The 1:2 memory allocation profile makes this instance cost-efficient for compute-bound parallel workloads that do not require high memory-per-core density. Evaluated benchmark metrics indicate strong suitability for software compilation (Geekbench compile score 9437.0), static web serving (9.0 GB/sec throughput), parallel batch processing, and in-memory key-value caching (Redis SET throughput of 10.16 million ops/sec).
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 12 vCPUs across 6 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores at 2.5 GHz, paired with 24.0 GB of memory. It features AVX-512 instruction support, 35 MB of L3 cache, and a 4 Gbps baseline network speed, with no local storage or GPUs attached. Benchmark results show average multi-core processing performance, indicated by a PassMark CPU score of 11934.41 and a Redis SET throughput of 10.16 million operations per second, alongside lower single-core compression speeds. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides balanced resource density for parallel compute tasks. It is well suited for software compilation, web serving, and multi-core batch processing workloads.
